analysis.title: GS Blekos - FED 3x Hikes / Siemens Energy / Zalando / On / ConvaTec / WOSG / Enagas / Consumer & Nielsen / Talanx / Coreweave 11 Nov 2026
key_insights: GS economists say the October CPI report surprised meaningfully to the upside across several categories and was a third month of worse inflation news.
GS still expects a second 25bp Fed hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike in March 2027. A January hike is possible but March is judged more likely.

GS expects the November and December inflation reports to be softer, then larger start-of-year price increases amid cost pressures to lift January inflation. This is the reason given for March over January.
Siemens Energy's announced buyback implies about €27bn of total returns of value (buyback plus dividends) out to FY 2030, versus Visible Alpha at €24bn and GSe at €30bn.

GS expects Siemens Energy's Capital Markets Day on 12 Nov to show a stronger profit outlook and a material acceleration in cash flow. Capital allocation out to FY 2028 is 1/3 capex, 1/3 returns of value, 1/3 retained, and GS expects this to change once FY 2030 guidance is added. GS remains Buy (on Conviction List).
Zalando CFO meeting: 4Q started well with autumn/winter trading on track. The three consumer apps overlap by only 10%, and management remains confident in a 3-4% retail media target by 2028.
Zalando management sees AI and agentic commerce as growth catalysts and an efficiency driver. B2B momentum continues with the Scayle pipeline full.

Zalando reiterated its 6-8% 2028 adj. EBIT margin target. Four building blocks: flat gross margin, overhead efficiencies, logistics network reshaping, and payment/commercial buying synergies from merging AY and Zalando.
On Holding 3Q26: constant-FX sales +17.8% y/y, underlying gross margin +320bps y/y, adj. EBITDA margin 21.9% excluding tariff refunds, in a promotional sportswear market.

On reported a strong improvement in US wholesale sell-out versus 2Q, healthy partner inventory, and exceptional early signals from the Cloud Surfer 3 launch with run specialty partners. The share of online customers under 24 almost doubled y/y.

GS sees multiple growth levers for On into 2027: refreshed running franchise with new superfoams, entry into Football and Golf, Sneaker share gains, and scaling apparel from a low base. Buy, 12m TP cut to $41 from $44.

ConvaTec: GS sees upside to the multiple alongside roughly mid-teens EPS growth over 12 months if the company executes on accelerating growth and handles cost inflation. Estimates broadly unchanged, PT 300p, Buy.
Watches of Switzerland 1H27 trading update: group revenue £974mn, +15% cFX, versus GSe £946mn and Visible Alpha consensus £941mn. US revenue +22% cFX to £501mn, UK +9% to £473mn.

Watches of Switzerland guides 1H27 pre-IFRS adjusted EBIT of £87-89mn (about +28%, margin +80-100bps) and raised the low end of FY27 guidance: cFX revenue growth 7-10% (was 5-10%), pre-IFRS 16 adj. EBIT margin expansion 60-80bps (was 40-80bps). PT 930p from 920p, Buy.
GS stays Sell on Enagas, saying structural headwinds still outweigh the positives.

CoreWeave 3Q26: stock up 8% after hours. Revenue 3% above the Street and EBIT margin 350bps above (Visible Alpha). 4Q implied revenue guidance is 3% above the Street, margin 100bps above, and capex 22% below.

CoreWeave financing plan: no additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027. Most remaining capital needs are to be funded through DDTLs (delayed-draw term loans) that can finance 70%-100% of associated capex at 7-10% yields.
The note also lists a Europe consumer products Nielsen read (Beiersdorf subdued, Cold/Flu accelerating in Consumer Health) and a Talanx 3Q26 earnings preview, with no detail in the text provided.

market_movers.rationale: Siemens Energy (ENR1n.DE, no US listing): GS sees the buyback as a positive signal of confidence in the outlook and expects a stronger profit outlook and cash flow acceleration at the Capital Markets Day. Name is on the Conviction List.
12m TP cut to $41 from $44. 3Q26 cFX sales +17.8% y/y, underlying gross margin +320bps, and improving US wholesale sell-out.
ConvaTec (CTEC.L, no US listing): upside to the multiple with mid-teens EPS growth if growth accelerates and cost inflation is managed. PT unchanged.
Watches of Switzerland (WOSG.L, no US listing): PT raised to 930p from 920p after 1H27 revenue of £974mn beat consensus of £941mn and the low end of FY27 guidance was raised.
Enagas (ENAG.MC, no US listing): structural headwinds still outweigh the positives.
Zalando (ZALG.DE, no US listing): CFO meeting reiterated the 6-8% 2028 adj. EBIT margin target and a good start to 4Q. The note does not state a rating or target in the text provided.

3Q26 revenue 3% and EBIT margin 350bps above the Street, with 4Q guidance above the Street and capex 22% below. The financing plan adds visibility, and GS frames it as a first step in a stock rerating.

sector_views.rationale: US Nielsen data shows Cold/Flu accelerating in Consumer Health while Beiersdorf remains subdued. The note gives no further detail.

earnings_insights: On Holding 3Q26 (reported): cFX sales +17.8% y/y, underlying gross margin +320bps y/y, adj. EBITDA margin 21.9% excluding tariff refunds.

Watches of Switzerland 1H27 trading update (reported): group revenue £974mn, +15% cFX, versus GSe £946mn and Visible Alpha consensus £941mn. US £501mn (+22% cFX), UK £473mn (+9%). Company guides 1H27 pre-IFRS adj. EBIT of £87-89mn (+28%).
Watches of Switzerland FY27 guidance raised at the low end: cFX revenue growth 7-10% (was 5-10%), pre-IFRS 16 adj. EBIT margin expansion 60-80bps (was 40-80bps).
CoreWeave 3Q26 (reported 11 Nov): revenue 3% above the Street and EBIT margin 350bps above (Visible Alpha). 4Q implied revenue guidance 3% above the Street, margin 100bps above, capex 22% below.
Zalando (CFO meeting, no print): management reiterated the 6-8% 2028 adj. EBIT margin target.
Talanx 3Q'26 earnings preview is listed in the note without figures in the text provided.

macro_indicators.reading: Surprised meaningfully to the upside across several categories, third month of worse inflation news
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS cites the upside surprise as the reason for adding a third Fed hike. No index values are given in the text.
GS's own forecast for the policy path.
GS says January is possible but March is more likely because it expects softer November and December inflation, then larger price increases at the start of 2027.

risk_factors: Inflation re-accelerating at the start of 2027 from ongoing cost pressures, which could bring the third hike forward to January.
Siemens Energy: capital allocation may prove conservative, and the allocation split is expected to change once FY 2030 guidance is added.
ConvaTec: execution on accelerating growth and navigating cost inflation.
Enagas: structural headwinds outweigh the positives (GS Sell).

tension_points.bull_case: Not applicable. The note is one-sided hawkish: three months of worse inflation news support a December hike and a third hike in March 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: GS expects softer November and December inflation reports, which is why it prefers March over January for the third hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Larger start-of-year price increases in January from ongoing cost pressures would pull the third hike forward to January.
